title: India's exports just jumped 23% in a single month. November 10, 2026.
excerpt: From a civil servant whose unjust dismissal launched Indian political organizing, to the first Sikh ever elected to Georgia's legislature, to a 23% year-on-year export surge, November 10's three stories are about turning setbacks and starting points into lasting institutions.
bodyHtml:
Today's stories span 178 years and two continents, but share a thread: each one is about someone - or something - built once and still standing on that foundation today.

He passed the toughest exam of the British Raj - then got dismissed on a technicality. It made him a founder of Indian politics

Surendranath Banerjee, born November 10, 1848, in Calcutta, passed the Indian Civil Service exam in 1869 but was dismissed in 1874 on a technicality. He founded the Indian Association in 1876, led it into the Indian National Congress in 1886, and became a leading voice against the 1905 Partition of Bengal.

His parents immigrated from India to Georgia. On November 3, 2026, he became the first Sikh ever elected to its state legislature

Jyot Singh, raised in Norcross, Georgia by Sikh and Punjabi immigrant parents from India, won Georgia House District 97 in the November 3, 2026 general election - the first Sikh American and first Indian American elected to the Georgia General Assembly.

India's exports just jumped 23% in a single month

India's merchandise exports rose 23.04% year-on-year to $44.40 billion in September 2026, per Commerce Ministry data, driven by engineering goods, electronics, petroleum products and chemicals. Cumulative exports for April-September this fiscal year reached $259.89 billion, up 18.51% year-on-year.

Three stories, one pattern: an unjust dismissal that built a movement, an immigrant family's story that built a legislator, and months of steady growth that built a trend.
